steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: On 23 August 1939, Nazi Germany and the Soviet Union signed a non-aggression pact in Moscow. The public agreement promised that neither side would attack the other for 10 years. A secret protocol divided eastern Europe into spheres of influence: Germany would get western Poland, and the USSR would get eastern Poland, Finland, Estonia, Latvia, and Bessarabia. This pact shocked the world - the two ideological enemies had made a deal. | Key Fact: At 4:45 am on 1 September 1939, the German battleship Schleswig-Holstein opened fire on the Polish garrison at Westerplatte in Danzig. Over 1.5 million German troops, with 2,500 tanks and 1,900 aircraft, invaded Poland from the north, south, and west. The attack used the "Blitzkrieg" (lightning war) tactic of rapid armoured advances support

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Explain why the Nazi-Soviet Pact was important. (4 marks) | How important was the Nazi-Soviet Pact in causing the outbreak of war in 1939? (8 marks) | "Appeasement was the main reason war broke out in 1939." How far do you agree? (12 marks)
